stem.text: ClOCCOCl can be used to make many polymers.

guidance: A ethdioyl (di)chloride, oxal(di)oyl (di)chloride, oxalic acid dichloride, oxalic dichloride

explanation.text: ClOCCOCl is two –COCl groups joined directly: the dioyl chloride of ethanedioic acid (HOOC–COOH). Its systematic name is ethanedioyl dichloride; the stem ‘ethane’ counts the two carbons and ‘dioyl chloride’ shows both ends are acyl chlorides.

reasoningChain: Recognise two C=O carbons, each with Cl: a dioyl dichloride.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing ethanoyl dichloride, which suggests one acyl group with two Cl atoms; the MS ignores it.
Writing dichloroethanal or another name that treats the C=O groups as aldehydes.

stem.text: ClOCCOCl reacts with H2N(CH2)4NH2 to form a polymer.
Draw a section of the polymer showing only one repeat unit.
Any functional groups should be fully displayed.

guidance: A [1] if NH has incorrect number of H’s.
A additional atoms if outside of bracketed repeat unit.
correct amide link should be attached to a C at each end, e.g. C–CO–NH–C, and not Cl–CO–NH–.

points.text: M2 exactly one RU, trailing bonds, no errors

figure.alt: From the MS: one repeat unit drawn as –C(=O)–C(=O)–N(H)–(CH2)4–N(H)– with the C=O and N–H bonds displayed and trailing bonds at both ends.

explanation.text: Each Cl of the dioyl chloride reacts with an NH<sub>2</sub> of the diamine, losing HCl and forming an amide link –CO–NH–. One repeat unit contains one of each monomer residue: –CO–CO–NH–(CH<sub>2</sub>)<sub>4</sub>–NH–, with trailing bonds at both ends.
‘Fully displayed’ means both C=O and N–H bonds are drawn out. A correct amide link must have carbon on both sides; an end group like Cl–CO–NH– does not count.

reasoningChain: Remove Cl from each end of the acid chloride and H from each NH<sub>2</sub>.
Draw –C(=O)–C(=O)–NH–(CH<sub>2</sub>)<sub>4</sub>–NH– with trailing bonds, displaying C=O and N–H.

inferredMistakes.text: Leaving Cl or H atoms at the ends of the repeat unit instead of trailing bonds.
Drawing two repeat units, or a unit that starts and ends in the middle of a monomer.
Writing –NH<sub>2</sub>– inside the chain, i.e. the wrong number of H on N.

stem.text: State the type of polymerisation involved and the linkage between the monomers.

explanation.text: Each new bond forms with loss of a small molecule (HCl), so it is condensation polymerisation. The new link is an amide, giving a polyamide. ‘Peptide’ is ignored because that name is used for links between amino acids.

reasoningChain: A small molecule (HCl) is lost each time: condensation.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing ‘addition’ because two monomers join, missing the loss of HCl.
Writing the formula CONH or ‘peptide’ instead of the word amide; the MS ignores both.

stem.text: When H<sub>2</sub>NCO(CH<sub>2</sub>)<sub>2</sub>CONH<sub>2</sub> reacts with a suitable reagent, H<sub>2</sub>N(CH<sub>2</sub>)<sub>4</sub>NH<sub>2</sub> forms.

guidance: (A H2 and Ni / Pt / Pd and Heat and pressure).

explanation.text: The starting compound is a diamide. Reducing both C=O groups to CH<sub>2</sub> converts each –CONH<sub>2</sub> into –CH<sub>2</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>, so the two CO carbons become the end CH<sub>2</sub> groups of H<sub>2</sub>N(CH<sub>2</sub>)<sub>4</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>. The syllabus reagent for reducing amides is LiAlH<sub>4</sub>, which is destroyed by water, so ‘(aq)’ contradicts the answer.

reasoningChain: Compare structures: C=O has become CH<sub>2</sub>, a reduction.

inferredMistakes.text: Giving NaBH<sub>4</sub>, which does not reduce amides.
Giving water or dilute acid, which would hydrolyse the amide instead of reducing it.

stem.text: Describe the reagents and conditions used.

explanation.text: Each C–Br is substituted by NH<sub>2</sub> through nucleophilic substitution by ammonia. The syllabus conditions are NH<sub>3</sub> in ethanol, heated under pressure (in a sealed tube) so that the volatile ammonia stays in the mixture. An excess of ammonia reduces further substitution to secondary amines.
The one mark needs all three: ammonia, heat and a sealed tube or pressure. Aqueous or alkaline conditions contradict the answer, because hydroxide would give the diol instead.

reasoningChain: Br → NH<sub>2</sub> at each end: nucleophilic substitution by NH<sub>3</sub>.
Conditions: heat in a sealed tube (under pressure), ammonia in ethanol.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing aqueous ammonia or NaOH(aq), which the MS treats as a contradiction.
Giving ammonia and heat but no sealed tube or pressure.
Giving KCN then reduction, which would add two carbons and give H<sub>2</sub>N(CH<sub>2</sub>)<sub>6</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>.

issues.note: QP 中 (b)(i) 与 (b) 同一行，'ClOCCOCl reacts with H2N(CH2)4NH2 to form a polymer.' 是 (i) 的第一句，所以 (b) 组本身没有 stem。
'oxal(di)oyl (di)chloride' 等名称照抄。10(c) Guidance 括号内 '(A H2 and Ni / Pt / Pd and Heat and pressure).' 原文就在括号里，照抄。
答案栏 'ammonia / heat / sealed tube/pressure' 原文分三行缩进排列，没有 and 或分隔符，写成一个 point：'ammonia heat sealed tube/pressure'，表示三项都要有才得 1 分（推断）。
